name: Texas Gas Fayetteville Lateral
researcher_notes: Not an existing row. The nearest rows are the Fayetteville Express line (P0189, a different 42 inch line) and the Texas Gas main line (P0263). This is a separate 36 inch lateral, so it is staged as a segment under the Texas Gas Transmission Pipeline name. Federal Register notice of 23 November 2007 (FERC docket CP07-417) gives 166.2 miles of 36 inch pipe from Conway County, Arkansas to Coahoma County, Mississippi, capacity about 841,000 MMBtu per day for the lateral, and two phases: first 66 miles, then 100 miles. A Talk Business article of 11 February 2008 gives the whole two-lateral project as about 821 million dollars; this cost covers the Greenville Lateral too, so it is a project-level figure and should be checked or dropped. Southwestern Energy's 2009 teleconference remarks say Phase 1 went into service on 24 December 2008 and Phase 2 on 1 April 2009, so status is operating. Start year 2008 is for Phase 1. Capacity was later raised to about 1.3 Bcf per day by added compression; that was not verified in a page, so the permitted 841,000 figure is staged. Proposal year 2006 comes from the December 2006 precedent agreement described in the Talk Business article. The reviewer may split into Phase 1 (66 mi, 2008) and Phase 2 (100 mi, 2009). Route not researched: set RouteType unavailable until FERC GIS is checked. Boardwalk Pipeline Partners is an exact gazetteer match; Texas Gas Transmission LLC is not in the gazetteer yet. Greenville Lateral is handled in the Gulf run. Single source states each value; the 2007 notice and the 2009 company remarks are independent publishers.
